top.line: Insure an agent row by row, under enforced controls
top.para: An agent behaviour policy already has the shape of an insurance policy: a limit for each risk it names, nothing for what it does not, and a lower premium for each enforced control. In a worked example, an uncontrolled agent pays £69,850 for £80,000 of cover; a controlled one, £6,720.

in-short.line: Ten lines from the house to the next article
in-short.para: An insurer de-risks an action under conditions and limits; the behaviour policy has rows; the insurance is one-to-one with them; the delta is uninsurable; the formula is deterministic; only enforced controls count; the runtime matters; premiums start high and fall; the vault simulates it.

house.line: A house policy has conditions, limits and exclusions
house.para: Home contents insurance asks about locks and location, caps any one item, usually between £1,000 and £2,500, asks for valuables to be declared, and at the claim checks the doors were locked. Agents need that same simple proposition, one agent at a time.

uninsurable.line: The delta is outside cover, and that is the point
uninsurable.para: The Licence to Operate vault's agent has a grant of 12 capabilities and a mandate of 4; the other 8 are in reach and covered by nothing. The bigger the reach, the more is uninsurable; customer records are uninsurable above 20 per action.

one-to-one.line: Each named risk gets its own limit
one-to-one.para: Corrupted records up to £20,000, leaked data up to £50,000, a wrong answer up to £10,000; shell access has no row, so it is excluded. A claim maps to a row, a row to its controls, a control to its log: a graph that can now be kept current.

formula.line: Six steps: exclude, rate, factor, runtime, premium, claim
formula.para: No limit means no cover; each row has a base rate; each enforced control multiplies it down; the runtime multiplies every row; premium is limit times rate; a claim pays if the conditions held. A prompt line gets a factor of 1: it held 3 of 12 attacks, a hook 12 of 12.

maximum.line: Uncontrolled costs 87% of the cover; controlled, 8%
maximum.para: An uncontrolled agent on an uncertified runtime pays £69,850 for £80,000 of cover, worth it only when cover is needed to operate. A certified runtime and five enforced controls take it to £6,720. That is how cyber insurance should have priced: on evidence, not a questionnaire.

measured.line: Motor, health and cyber already price on measurement
measured.para: Black boxes measure speed, braking and cornering and set the renewal price; medical underwriting sets cover by preconditions; Coalition scans instead of asking; Munich Re prices model performance. Agents log every call, so the data exists; the mapping to rows is missing.

where.line: The runtime is a condition, and so is the licence
where.para: Certification of the runtime and of the enforcing software lowers the price; an uncertified runtime raises it or ends cover. A licence to operate, four facts and a date, could be a condition of cover, and a change of runtime a reason to look again.

licence.line: The vault already simulates a licence and a premium
licence.para: Vault posrhzp3 holds a rate table: a band, an ask threshold, a ceiling per action, a pool with a reserve, and a premium per interval. Each reply in its support conversation shows its cost first; licence, mandate, payment and cover can each be lost. In credits, not money.

vendors.line: Vendors already cover some things, on conditions
vendors.para: Microsoft's copyright commitment applies only if the customer used its guardrails: the locked door again. Intercom backs Fin with up to $1M; ElevenLabs has an AIUC-1-backed policy; Munich Re offers vendors performance warranties. None is yet a payout per row.

next.line: Who can underwrite it, the vendors' share, a vault
next.para: The series continues with a research brief on who can underwrite an agent behaviour policy today, then what agent vendors should cover themselves, then the formula as a vault with a premium calculator for your own agent, now vault m1wbrefr.

limits.line: Illustrative numbers, no insurer, a sketch of a formula
limits.para: The factors are not fitted to loss data; no insurer has agreed to this; the formula ignores interactions and correlated losses; runtime certification does not exist in this form; the vault is a simulation; the other insurance lines are analogies.

sources.line: A memo, a script, the vault and dated sources
sources.para: From Dinis's memo of 28 October 2026; the formula and numbers from premium.py and its data file; the Licence to Operate vault and RiskMandate's pages read that day; outside sources fetched by a research agent, with the health paragraph paraphrased.
